title: Architecture — Architecture
text:
COFA FORWARD is a modular Python application (Streamlit UI) for weather
operations and anticipatory climate intelligence over the Freely Associated
States (Palau, FSM, RMI). It is a single-developer-friendly, single-process app
with no microservices and no required credentials.

title: Architecture — Design principles
text:
1. **One data foundation, two modes.** Weather Operations and Anticipatory
   Intelligence share the same geographic registry, observations/forecasts,
   source/timestamp metadata, map framework, island profiles, impact catalog,
   and uncertainty framework.
2. **Deterministic science first.** Every quantitative indicator is a tested
   numerical function. A language model (optional, not enabled by default) may
   only *explain* validated results — never compute them.
3. **Provenance everywhere.** Derived values record their inputs, methods,
   parameters, baselines, aggregation, and missing-data handling.
4. **Never fabricate.** Missing data stays missing; no invented storms,
   warnings, forecasts, probabilities, or impact counts.

title: Architecture — Package layout
text:
```
config/          YAML (app, geography, sources, enso, drought, cyclones, alerts)
src/cofa_forward/
  config.py        validated config loader (pydantic-backed schemas)
  units.py         explicit metric<->imperial conversions
  timeutil.py      UTC timestamp normalization
  schemas.py       pydantic models (GeoEntity, SourceRecord, EnsoEpisode, ...)
  sample_data.py   deterministic synthetic sample data (clearly labeled)
  ingestion/       provider adapters (base + Open-Meteo forecast/archive + stubs)
  storage/         FileCache, SQLite Database, ParquetStore, provenance
  geography/       registry, spatial attribution (haversine), aggregation
  climate/         ENSO state, episodes, analogs, climatology
  drought/         rainfall metrics, anomalies, percentiles, SPI, freshwater, alerts
  cyclones/        tracks, proximity, climatology, ENSO analysis, exposure
  impacts/         event catalog, evidence labeling
  intelligence/    indicators, synthesis, confidence, report builder
  visualization/   maps (Plotly scattergeo), charts, legends, layers
  ui/              Streamlit app + 9 pages + shared components
scripts/          initialize_data, ingest_weather, ingest_rainfall, ...
tests/            unit + integration + scientific regression (pytest)
```

title: Architecture — Data flow
text:
```
providers --(ingestion adapters)--> FileCache --> normalize/validate
      |                                    |
      +-- provenance/ingestion history --> SQLite (data/catalog.db)
                                           |
computed indicators/analogs <-- drought/climate/cyclone modules
      |
      +--> ui/ (Streamlit) & intelligence/report_builder (Markdown brief)
```

* `data/raw` — untouched source data
* `data/interim` — intermediate transforms
* `data/processed` — normalized analytical datasets
* `data/samples` — clearly labeled synthetic data
* `data/cache` — TTL cache for remote fetches

title: Architecture — Key decisions
text:
* **Maps use Plotly `scattergeo`** (no Mapbox token, no tile API key) so the app
  runs fully offline with built-in Natural Earth coastlines. A heavier map stack
  (PyDeck/Folium) is a later option if richer base layers are needed.
* **Geography is point-based seed data.** Boundaries/polygons (GeoPandas/Shapely)
  are deferred; the registry is data-driven so a validated inventory can replace
  the seed YAML without code changes.
* **Spatial attribution is nearest-grid-cell**, recorded explicitly, and never
  described as downscaling.
* **Percentile drought indicators before SPI.** A non-parametric normal-score
  SPI is available; full gamma-fit SPI is deferred.

title: Architecture — Extending
text:
Add a provider: subclass `ingestion.base.BaseAdapter`, implement `fetch`/
normalization, add a row to `config/sources.yaml`, and set its status honestly.
Add a location: append an entity to `config/geography.yaml`.

title: Data_Dictionary — Geography registry (`config/geography.yaml`)
text:
| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| geo_id | str | Stable identifier (e.g. `PAL`, `FSM-CHUUK`, `RMI-MAJ`). |
| name | str | Display name. |
| entity_type | str | `country`, `state`, `island`, `atoll`, `monitoring_location`. |
| country_code | str | ISO-3166 alpha-2 (PW / FM / MH). |
| parent_geo_id | str | Parent entity id (null for countries). |
| latitude / longitude | float | Approximate point location (seed, not surveyed). |
| area_km2 | float | Approximate area (seed). |
| population / population_year | int | Approximate population (seed). |
| population_source | str | Provenance of the population figure. |
| data_coverage | str | Qualitative coverage (moderate / sparse). |
| notes | str | Caveats. |

> The registry is **seed data** (`status: seed`). A validated FAS island/atoll
> inventory can replace it without code changes.

title: Data_Dictionary — Weather forecast (`open-meteo-forecast`)
text:
Hourly/daily DataFrames; metric units (°C, mm, m/s, hPa, %). Key columns:
`temperature_2m`, `precipitation`, `relative_humidity_2m`, `wind_speed_10m`,
`wind_direction_10m`, `surface_pressure`, `precipitation_sum` (daily),
`precipitation_probability_max` (daily). Metadata includes `latitude`,
`longitude`, `elevation_m`, `timezone`, and attribution note.

title: Data_Dictionary — Historical rainfall (`open-meteo-archive`)
text: Daily `precip_mm` Series (mm), tz-aware UTC, with NaN for missing days.

title: Data_Dictionary — Derived indicators
text:
| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `rain_{n}m_mm` | Rolling n-month rainfall total (n ∈ 1,3,6,12); NaN if any month incomplete. |
| `anomaly_mm` | Monthly total − calendar-month climatology (baseline-valid only). |
| `anomaly_pct` | (obs − clim) / clim × 100. |
| `percentile` | Empirical percentile of the month vs its calendar-month baseline distribution. |
| `percentile_category` | Severity label from percentile bins (config). |

title: Data_Dictionary — Provenance record
text:
Every derived value records: `dataset_id`, `source_url`, `retrieved_at`,
`valid_time`, `init_time`, `lead_time`, `calculation_method`, `parameters`,
`baseline_period`, `geographic_aggregation`, `missing_data_handling`,
`output_timestamp`, `code_version`, `notes`.

title: Data_Sources — Data Sources
text:
Status values: `implemented_and_tested`, `implemented_but_not_verified`,
`requires_credentials`, `requires_manual_import`, `planned`, `unavailable`.
A source is marked `implemented_and_tested` only after a successful integration
test. This catalog was refreshed with extensive online research on 2026-10-28
(five independent research passes over ENSO, cyclones, precipitation/drought,
exposure/terrain, and AI-forecast access).

title: Data_Sources — Implemented & tested (live adapters)
text:
| Source | Endpoint | Auth | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Open-Meteo Forecast** | `api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast` | none | current + hourly + daily, 16-day horizon, ~11 km; **multi-model** via `models=` (ECMWF IFS/AIFS, GFS, ICON, GEM) |
| **Open-Meteo Historical (ERA5)** | `archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive` | none | daily precipitation, ~25 km |
| **NOAA CPC Oceanic Niño Index** | `cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/data/indices/oni.ascii.txt` | none | authoritative ENSO index; phase derived via CPC ≥5-season criterion |
| **IBTrACS v04r01 (WP basin)** | `ncei.noaa.gov/.../csv/ibtracs.WP.list.v04r01.csv` | none | historical tracks, 1842–present (114 MB CSV) |
| **JMA RSMC Tokyo (active storms)** | `jma.go.jp/bosai/typhoon/data/targetTc.json` → `specifications.json` | none | position, 10-min wind, pressure, 5-day forecast + probability circles |
| **CHIRPS v3 (precipitation)** | `data.chc.ucsb.edu/products/CHIRPS/v3.0/monthly/global/cogs/` | none | monthly COGs, 0.05°, point extraction via rasterio range requests |

`ingest_ibtracs.py`, `ingest_jma.py`, `check_sources.py`. Live tests:
`uv run pytest -m network` (6 tests, all passing).

title: Data_Sources — ENSO & seasonal climate
text:
* **CPC ONI** (`oni.ascii.txt`) — the canonical index. Free, no auth, plain ASCII,
  monthly, 1950–present. **Implemented.**
* **CPC ENSO Diagnostic Discussion** (`enso_advisory/ensodisc.html`) — the official
  status statement (Watch/Advisory) + probabilistic outlook. Narrative HTML, monthly
  (~2nd Thursday). *Planned* (regex-scrape alert status + synopsis).
* **PEAC** (`weather.gov/peac/`) — FAS-specific seasonal rainfall outlook
  (14 stations incl. Koror/Yap/Chuuk/Pohnpei/Kosrae/Kwajalein/Majuro), monthly.
  HTML tables; *note: fetched page still showed SON-2024 → add a freshness guard*.
* **NMME** (`ftp.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/International/nmme/netcdf/`) — gridded 1° seasonal
  forecasts (NetCDF3), monthly inits, 2011–present. **Implemented** (xarray +
  netCDF4, 6-model ensemble mean + spread, wired into ENSO & Climate page).
  IRI Data Library now requires login; CPC FTP + AWS `s3://noaa-nmme-pds` are open.
* **IRI ENSO plume** — *no longer serves numeric data* (figure only since ~Sep 2026).
  Not a viable numeric dependency.

title: Data_Sources — Tropical cyclones
text:
* **IBTrACS v04r01** (`WP` basin CSV/NetCDF) — multi-agency best tracks.
  **Implemented.** WMO wind/pressure = responsible agency (JMA 10-min for WP);
  per-agency `USA_WIND`/`TOKYO_WIND` retained so averaging periods stay explicit.
* **JMA RSMC Tokyo** JSON (`targetTc.json`, `specifications.json`, `forecast.json`,
  `pastTracks.json`) — authoritative active-storm source. **Implemented.**
* **JTWC** text warnings (`tgftp.nws.noaa.gov/data/raw/wt/wtpn3x.pgtw..txt`) — 1-min
  wind + quadrant radii + forecast track. **Implemented** (full ATCF-text parser).
* **NWS Guam / PEAC** (`wtpq3x.pgum.*`, `api.weather.gov/alerts`) — FAS island-specific
  watches/warnings. **Implemented** (TCP parser `nws_guam.py`; `api.weather.gov/
  alerts` available for structured zone alerts).
* ⚠️ Wind-speed averaging differs by agency (JMA 10-min vs JTWC/NWS 1-min). Always
  carry the agency + averaging period with any wind value.

title: Data_Sources — Satellite imagery
text:
* **Himawari-9** (JMA/NICT real-time web) — full-disk visible composite, 10-min
  cadence. **Implemented** (latest full-disk tile shown on the Tropical Cyclones
  page). IR bands and region-zoom tiles are a follow-up.
* **GOES** (NOAA) — *not a fit for the FAS*: GOES-West covers the eastern Pacific/
  Americas; the FAS (130–175E) is in Himawari's domain.
* **Sentinel-2/3** (Copernicus, free) and **VIIRS** (NASA/NOAA, Earthdata) — ocean/
  land remote sensing (SST, ocean colour, vegetation), not weather feeds; heavy
  raster. *Planned* for SST/coastal overlays (STAC/AWS/LANCE access documented).

title: Data_Sources — Precipitation & drought
text:
* **CHIRPS v3** (`data.chc.ucsb.edu/products/CHIRPS/v3.0/`) — **implemented** (point
  extraction from monthly COGs via rasterio range requests). 0.05°, 60N–60S, CC BY 4.0.
  **Land-masked** → sub-pixel islands use a documented max-valid-pixel heuristic; ERA5
  is preferred for ocean-adjacent atolls.
* **NASA GPM IMERG** (GES DISC) — global incl. ocean, 0.1°, sub-daily.
  **Implemented & tested** (`earthaccess` adapter `ingestion/imerg.py` for daily
  point extraction; live-verified with an Earthdata bearer token). Requires
  `EARTHDATA_TOKEN` (or `.netrc`) + a one-time GPM IMERG EULA acceptance.
  Note V07→V08 transition (V07 Final ends Sep 2025).
* **PERSIANN-CDR** (NOAA NCEI) — 0.25° daily, 1983–present, no login.
* **GPCC** (DWD) — gauge-only land; essentially no FAS gauges → *not recommended*.
* **USGS P1RXUMV3** (western-Pacific drought + 7-day GFS forecast) — covers **FSM,
  RMI, Nauru, Solomon — Palau NOT included**. ScienceBase blocks non-browser GET.
  Reuse its R scripts to replicate the IMERG-Early-Run + GFS pipeline for Palau.
* **SPEIbase / SPEI monitor** — global land 0.5°/1° (ODbL); many FAS atolls fall
  between cells. Better to compute SPI/SPEI ourselves from CHIRPS/IMERG (SPI is
  already implemented in `drought/spi.py`).

title: Data_Sources — Population, boundaries, terrain, infrastructure
text:
* **WorldPop** (`data.worldpop.org/.../Global_2000_2020_1km/`) — **implemented** (point/radius
  extraction via rasterio). CC BY 4.0, ~1 km, 2000–2020, covers PLW/FSM/MHL, no login.
  UN-adjusted 2020 totals exceed censuses → used for **spatial exposure**, not as the
  census of record. (WOPR does *not* cover these countries.)
* **GPWv4** (SEDAC) — ~1 km, requires Earthdata Login; census-consistent cross-check.
* **HDX COD-AB boundaries** — FSM (`cod-ab-fsm`) and RMI (`cod-ab-mhl`), CC BY-IGO,
  reviewed Oct 2024. **Implemented** (loaded via `pyshp` + `rasterio`, no GDAL/
  geopandas) — enables accurate zonal WorldPop population per atoll/state.
  **Palau** (no COD-AB) uses **geoBoundaries ADM1** (16 states, ODbL/OSM), parsed
  from GeoJSON — also implemented.
* **Copernicus DEM GLO-30/GLO-90** (AWS Open Data, no login) — DSM terrain.
* **GEBCO** (CC BY 4.0) — 15 arc-sec topography+bathymetry (atoll coastal exposure).
* **SRTM GL1** (30 m) — via OpenTopography S3 or Earthdata (login).
* **OSM / Geofabrik / HOT** (ODbL) — the only open infrastructure/POI layer; coverage
  is uneven (Koror/Majuro/Pohnpei well mapped, outer atolls thin).

title: Data_Sources — AI / global forecast models
text:
* **Google WeatherNext 3** — allowlist-gated (free Google account, ~5–7 day approval),
  Zarr v3 / BigQuery / Earth Engine, 0.05°/0.1°/0.25°, hourly, 64-member, 15-day.
  Real-time data under an experimental ToU; historical (≥1 h old) is CC BY 4.0.
  **Adapter implemented** (`ingestion/weathernext.py`): reports `requires_credentials`
  and reads Zarr via `gcsfs` once the allowlist is granted. Access form submitted
  (see below).
* **NVIDIA Earth-2 / FourCastNet / StormCast** — open downloadable weights (NGC/HF,
  self-host on GPU via Modulus) or hosted NIM microservices (paid API key / DGX Cloud).
  **No keyless free hosted weather API.** Adapter implemented and reports honestly.
* **ECMWF AIFS open data** (`s3://ecmwf-forecasts`, CC BY 4.0, no account) — 0.25°,
  4×/day to 15 days, GRIB2. **Best free AI/global drop-in** (per-point via
  `ecmwf-opendata`).
* **NOAA GFS/GEFS** (NOMADS / AWS NODD `s3://noaa-gfs-bdp-pds`) — public domain,
  0.25°, byte-range GRIB2 subsetting. **Free fallback.**

title: Data_Sources — AI-model account status
text:
* **WeatherNext 3**: the access form requires (1) a Google account email, (2) a
  Google Cloud account email to be allowlisted, (3) name/country/organisation. The
  approval is 5–7 business days at Google's discretion. **Not yet granted.**
* **NVIDIA**: a free `build.nvidia.com` key covers LLM/vision/embedding NIMs, **not**
  the weather microservices (those need DGX Cloud). Signing up would not unblock a
  hosted weather feed, so it is not pursued.

title: Data_Sources — Requested but not freely accessible
text:
* **Windy** — commercial API only (`api.windy.com`); no free tier. Equivalent model
  data (ECMWF/GFS/ICON/GEM) is already integrated via Open-Meteo multi-model.
* **Weather Underground** — the free API was discontinued (2023); commercial only.
* **Meteoconsult** — no public free API, limited Pacific coverage.
* **NOAA US Drought Monitor (USDM)** — **US-only** (does not cover Palau/FSM/RMI).
  The app computes an internal precipitation-percentile **D0–D4** drought level
  instead, and uses CHIRPS/IMERG/ERA5 for drought indicators.

title: Data_Sources — Maps & basemaps
text:
The original Plotly `scattergeo` map showed the FAS atolls as invisible dots on a
blank ocean. Replaced with interactive Leaflet (folium) maps using **keyless
satellite basemaps** so the islands are actually visible:

* **Esri World Imagery** — high-res commercial-satellite mosaic (zoom 19); default.
* **NASA GIBS** BlueMarble / MODIS Terra / MODIS Aqua / VIIRS — official NASA EOSDIS
  daily true-colour (~250 m), no key. Tile-matrix-set names are layer-specific
  (`GoogleMapsCompatible_Level8/9`).
* **OpenStreetMap** — street fallback.

Basemaps are chosen client-side via a Leaflet layer control; tiles load in the
browser directly from GIBS/Esri (no server-side proxy, no credentials).

title: Data_Sources — Attribution & license notes
text:
Open-Meteo (CC BY 4.0), ERA5 (CC BY 4.0 via CDS), CHIRPS v3 (CC BY 4.0), WorldPop
(CC BY 4.0), GPWv4 (CC BY 4.0), GEBCO (CC BY 4.0), AIFS (CC BY 4.0). NOAA/NCEP/NCEI,
USGS, NASA, JTWC, NWS, JMA observational data are public-domain/observational.
SPEIbase is ODbL 1.0; HDX COD-AB is CC BY-IGO; OSM/Geofabrik/HOT are ODbL.
WeatherNext 3 real-time data is under a restrictive experimental ToU (historical is
CC BY 4.0). Always confirm each source's terms before redistribution.

title: Handoff — ⚠️ Environment note (RESOLVED 2026-10-28)
text:
A machine-wide DNS outage hit mid-build and has since been **resolved**. Kept for
reference:

- Root cause was: **Tailscale client (1.94.2) stale vs daemon (1.104.2)** → MagicDNS
  (resolver `100.100.100.100`) stopped forwarding → system resolver stuck → `uv`
  panicked (`system-configuration` crate reads a NULL) and `curl`/`pip`/`requests`
  DNS lookups failed.
- Fix applied: `tailscale set --accept-dns=false` (reverted system DNS to
  `1.1.1.1`/`8.8.8.8`); the machine owner later upgraded Tailscale.
- **Current status: `uv` works, DNS resolves, `uv.lock` is reconciled (pyshp is
  in it).** `uv run pytest`, `uv sync`, `uv run streamlit` all work normally.
- If `uv` ever panics again with `system-configuration … Attempted to create a
  NULL object`, it is the same network/Tailscale issue — check `tailscale status`
  for a client/daemon version mismatch and upgrade/restart Tailscale.
- No sudo available ("you do not exist in the passwd database" — shell runs as
  UID 501). Download workaround (if DNS is ever flaky): `dig +short @8.8.8.8
  <host>` then `curl --resolve "<host>:443:<IP>" ...`. HDX downloads also need a
  `--resolve` for `s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` (HDX redirects there via presigned
  URL).

title: Handoff — Key scientific/engineering decisions (do not regress)
text:
1. **Never fabricate.** Missing data stays missing; no invented storms/warnings/
   probabilities/impact counts. ENSO phase is derived from ONI and labeled as
   derived (official status = CPC discussion, ingested by the bulletin monitor).
2. **Provenance everywhere.** Derived values carry dataset/timestamp/method/
   baseline/aggregation. Stored in SQLite `data/catalog.db`.
3. **Units:** metric for science, imperial presentation-only (`units.py`).
4. **Spatial attribution ≠ downscaling.** Nearest-grid-cell only; the app always
   says "regional model estimate; individual-atoll conditions may differ."
5. **Percentile indicators before SPI** (gamma SPI now implemented in
   `drought/spi.py` — validated against reference values).
6. **Water balance is modeled** (`drought/water_balance.py`): documented planning
   defaults (100 L/person/day, 10 m²/person catchment, 0.8 eff), never claims
   actual shortage.
7. **CHIRPS land-mask heuristic:** max-valid-pixel in a 5×5 window (documented;
   ERA5 preferred for ocean-adjacent atolls).
8. **WorldPop is UN-adjusted** — use zonal (boundary) sum as the accurate method;
   census seed figures are the atoll total of record.
9. **Map = Plotly `scattergeo`** (no Mapbox token / tile key). Boundaries are not
   yet rendered as polygons on the map (only used for zonal stats).

title: Handoff — Gotchas
text:
- **Page modules MUST NOT live in a directory named `pages/`.** Streamlit
  1.66 auto-detects `pages/` next to the main script as a *multipage* app and
  `exec`s each file standalone, breaking relative imports (`ImportError:
  attempted relative import with no known parent package`) — the shell renders
  but no data loads. They live in `ui/sections/` for this reason. (`AppTest`
  won't catch this; only a real `streamlit run` browser does.)
- `scripts/verify_pages.py` (AppTest) times out when DNS is down because live
  fetches retry slowly; it passed cleanly (10/10) when network was up.
- IBTrACS CSV is ~114 MB; the network test downloads it (marked `network`).
- `monthly_totals` drops timezone before `to_period("M")` (avoids a pandas warning).
- The app's cached helpers (`ui/state.py`) use `st.cache_data` with TTLs — real
  rainfall/CHIRPS/WorldPop/boundaries are fetched once and cached (24h), so first
  load can be slow (CHIRPS full baseline ~1–2 min).

title: Macos_App — COFA FORWARD — macOS app (SwiftUI shell + offline cache)
text:
A native macOS app for the MacBook Pro that runs the full COFA FORWARD Streamlit
dashboard locally, with an offline snapshot so it works **anytime** — with or
without a network connection.

title: Macos_App — Architecture
text:
```
COFA Forward.app (SwiftUI, arm64, macOS 14+)
  ├─ WKWebView  ── loads http://127.0.0.1:8501
  ├─ ServerManager ── launches `.venv/bin/streamlit run …` (or `uv run streamlit`)
  │                    as a child process; sets COFA_OFFLINE=1 when toggled
  └─ "Refresh snapshot" ── runs `scripts/prefetch_snapshot.py`
```

The app is a **thin shell** — it does not reimplement any science. All 12 pages,
the Python deterministic-science layer, and the folium maps run in the bundled
Streamlit app; the Swift layer only hosts the process + web view and controls
offline mode.

title: Macos_App — Offline cache
text:
`COFA_OFFLINE=1` (set by the app's Offline toggle) switches the app to read the
pre-fetched snapshot instead of the network:

| Mechanism | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `FileCache(serve_stale=True)` | every adapter that goes through `make_cache()` (ENSO, ENSO discussion, JMA, JTWC, NWS Guam, PEAC, forecast, ERA5 archive) serves its cached raw responses past their TTL |
| `data/raw/` | WorldPop rasters, boundary SHP/GeoJSON, NMME NetCDF, IBTrACS CSV — downloaded once, re-read locally |
| `data/snapshot/` | structured per-source JSON/Parquet (CHIRPS monthly series per location, Himawari PNG, population, NMME) + `manifest.json` |

The snapshot is produced by `scripts/prefetch_snapshot.py` (run when online):

```bash
uv run python scripts/prefetch_snapshot.py --skip-ibtracs   # all locations
uv run python scripts/prefetch_snapshot.py --locations RMI-MAJ
```

The manifest records what was captured and when; a source that failed to fetch is
recorded as **missing** (never fabricated) and surfaced on the Data Sources page.

title: Macos_App — Offline map tiles
text:
`scripts/prefetch_tiles.py` downloads OpenStreetMap tiles (region z0-9 + a window
around each location at z10-11) into `data/tiles/`, and `cofa_forward.tileserver`
serves them on `127.0.0.1:8502`. In offline mode the map's "OpenStreetMap
(streets)" basemap is swapped to the local server, so the map *and* its imagery
work without a connection.

```bash
uv run python scripts/prefetch_tiles.py
uv run python -m cofa_forward.tileserver          # the macOS app starts this automatically
```

OSM is used for offline imagery because it is openly licensed (ODbL, attribution
required), permits caching for light personal use, and reaches high zoom. The
satellite basemaps (Esri/GIBS) are **not** cached offline — Esri restricts bulk
caching and GIBS true-colour caps at ~zoom 9 where atolls are only a few pixels.

title: Scientific_Methods — Rainfall accumulation
text:
Daily rainfall is summed to monthly totals; a month is valid only if at least
80% of its days are present (`min_days_frac`). Incomplete months become NaN —
**never zero**. Rolling n-month totals require all n contributing months to be
valid; otherwise the total is NaN.

title: Scientific_Methods — Climatology & anomalies
text:
* **Baseline:** 1991–2020 (configurable in `config/drought.yaml`).
* **Climatology:** mean rainfall per calendar month over the baseline.
* **Anomaly (mm):** observed − climatology. **Anomaly (%):** (obs − clim)/clim × 100.
* **Baseline validity:** an anomaly is computed only when ≥ `baseline_min_years`
  (default 15) years of valid data exist in the baseline; otherwise it is NaN and
  flagged.

title: Scientific_Methods — Percentile indicators
text:
The empirical percentile of a month against its calendar-month baseline
distribution uses midpoint ranking: (count < value + 0.5 × count == value) / n.
Severity bins are configurable (`config/drought.yaml`). Percentile indicators are
implemented **before** SPI per the build plan.

title: Scientific_Methods — Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI)
text:
`drought/spi.py` provides a non-parametric **normal-score transform**: the
empirical percentile mapped to a standard-normal quantile via the stdlib
`statistics.NormalDist`. It is a transparent approximation, **not** a full
gamma-fit SPI, and does not measure water availability directly. Full gamma-fit
SPI (with zero-precipitation and fitting handling) is a documented follow-up and
is disabled by default.

title: Scientific_Methods — Spatial attribution
text:
* **Nearest-grid-cell** extraction (haversine, km) attributes model grid data to
  a registry point.
* This is **attribution of existing model data**, not downscaling. No output is
  labeled statistically or dynamically downscaled, because no downscaling is
  performed.
* A coarse grid cell over an atoll is never presented as atoll-accurate; the UI
  shows "regional model estimate; individual-atoll conditions may differ."

title: Scientific_Methods — Tropical cyclones
text:
* **Distance** uses great-circle haversine (R = 6371.0088 km).
* **Proximity exposure** reports closest approach; it is **not** a wind-impact
  estimate (which needs storm size, intensity, and track uncertainty).
* **ENSO-conditioned analysis** reports counts with sample sizes and limitations;
  no causal claim is made from correlation and no hard-coded multiplier is turned
  into an operational risk probability.

title: Scientific_Methods — Historical analogs
text:
Analogs are ranked by a weighted, normalized absolute-distance similarity over
ENSO phase/intensity and rainfall anomaly (see `climate/analogs.py`). Missing
features are excluded and reported. A historical analog is **contextual
evidence, not a forecast**.

title: Scientific_Methods — Confidence labels
Scientific_Methods — Freshwater vulnerability
text:
Meteorological drought, hydrological stress, reported shortage, and modeled
future risk are separate concepts. A composite score is not computed unless all
required inputs exist; otherwise meteorological indicators are shown and missing
inputs are listed explicitly.

title: Scientific_Methods — Water-need forecast (modeled water balance)
text:
A deterministic water-balance model estimates, per island/atoll, whether forecast
rainfall over the next N days meets the population's water demand:

* daily demand (L) = population × `per_capita_lpd`
* catchment area (m²) = population × `per_person_catchment_m2`
* daily supply (L) = forecast precip (mm) × catchment (m²) × efficiency
  (1 mm over 1 m² = 1 L)
* required rainfall (mm) = total demand / (catchment × efficiency)
* balance (mm) = forecast rainfall − required rainfall (negative → projected deficit)

Defaults (`config/drought.yaml → freshwater.water_balance`): 100 L/person/day,
10 m²/person catchment, 0.8 collection efficiency, storage assumed 0
(conservative). These are **documented planning defaults, not measured site
data**; actual catchment, storage, desalination, and abstraction data are listed
as missing. The output is a **modeled rainfall-driven deficit/surplus**, never a
claim of actual water shortage.

title: Scientific_Methods — Bulletin monitoring
text:
Authoritative sources that publish regular public bulletins (rather than stable
APIs) are polled by `ingestion/bulletins.py`: content is fetched, hashed, and —
on change — parsed into a structured summary, snapshotted to `data/raw/bulletins/`,
and logged as an update. Parsers cover NWS/JTWC WMO text products (header, agency,
issue time, headline), JMA typhoon bulletins, and the CPC ENSO Diagnostic
Discussion (the official ENSO alert status). See `docs/DATA_SOURCES.md`.

title: Security — Security
text:
The initial release is a **local, single-user** application. Sensible defaults
are in place and documented so a remote deployment is not accidentally exposed.

title: Security — In place
text:
* Binds to `127.0.0.1` by default (never public).
* No credentials required to launch; `data/`, `data/cache/`, `.env`, and secrets
  are git-ignored.
* Secrets are read only from environment variables / `~/.config`-style files, and
  are **never** written to logs, reports, or the UI.
* External data is validated before processing (normalization + pydantic schemas);
  network fetches use timeouts and bounded retries with backoff.
* No arbitrary shell execution from UI controls.
* Retrieved documents and any future LLM output are treated as **untrusted data**:
  they can never override system behavior, execute code, or trigger tools.
* Errors are logged without secrets.
* Source data (`raw`) is kept separate from derived data (`processed`).

* **App service** — `com.ben.cofaforward-dashboard` runs Streamlit bound to
  `127.0.0.1:8501` (never a public bind).
* **Tunnel** — `cofaforward.benigmatic.com` → `http://127.0.0.1:8501` on the

* **TLS** — terminated by Cloudflare (HTTPS).
* **Secrets** — the Earthdata token lives at `~/.config/cofa-forward/earthdata_token`

Protected by **Cloudflare Access** (mirrors `ben.benigmatic.com`):

* Access app `COFA Forward` on `cofaforward.benigmatic.com`, policy `owner`

An optional **application-level password gate** remains in `app.py` (disabled

title: Analysis Roadmap — Analysis roadmap — what else would benefit COFA FORWARD
text:
Deep-dive into the tool's remaining gaps, framed by its real job: **anticipatory
water security and climate-hazard early warning for atoll nations** (Palau, FSM,
RMI). Each item is scored for value, feasibility, and effort, with the honest
caveat. Data sources are named and their free/open status noted.

title: Analysis Roadmap — The core insight
text:
The tool's three structural weaknesses are, in order:

1. **No ground truth.** Every layer is model (ERA5, NMME) or satellite (CHIRPS,
   IMERG, Himawari). The FAS has airport weather stations — the only independent
   check on all of it — and they are not yet wired in.
2. **Precipitation-only drought.** Drought is a *water balance* (precip minus
   evapotranspiration), but the monitor only sees the precip side. The USGS
   release this app now mirrors actually ships an ET + water-budget component
   (SSEBop) that is missing here.
3. **The two biggest atoll hazards are under-served.** Sea-level rise / king-tide
   flooding and cyclone *wind/surge impact* — not just track proximity — are what
   actually damage atolls, and neither is modeled yet.

---

title: Analysis Roadmap — Priority 1 — In-situ station ground truth (GHCNd)
text:
* **What:** daily precipitation + temperature from the FAS airport WMO stations
  (Koror PTRO, Yap PTYA, Chuuk PTKK, Pohnpei PTPN, Kosrae PTSA, Majuro PKMR,
  Kwajalein PKWA).
* **Why:** the single highest-value addition. It lets the app (a) validate
  ERA5/CHIRPS/IMERG against reality, (b) show a "satellite vs gauge" bias, and
  (c) feed the forecast-verification loop. Today every "drought" call is an
  unverified satellite/model estimate.
* **Source:** NOAA NCEI GHCNd (free, public domain, daily, 1900s–present).
* **Effort:** moderate (adapter + bias comparison + provenance). **Feasibility: high.**

title: Analysis Roadmap — Priority 2 — Evapotranspiration → true water balance (SSEBop)
text:
* **What:** operational actual ET (SSEBop) + water-balance = precipitation − ET
  per island, giving a real water-deficit drought indicator instead of a rainfall
  one.
* **Why:** this is the "Water Budget components" child of the same USGS release
  (Senay et al. 2026) the app now mirrors for rainfall. It converts "is it dry?"
  into "is there actually a water deficit?"
* **Source:** USGS SSEBop (1 km, global, 2000–present, free, already used by the
  same USGS team).
* **Effort:** moderate. **Feasibility: high.**

title: Analysis Roadmap — Priority 3 — Sea level + coastal flooding
text:
* **What:** satellite-altimetry sea-level anomaly + (optionally) tide/king-tide
  forecasts per atoll.
* **Why:** ENSO moves western-Pacific sea level by ±20–30 cm; on a 2 m atoll that
  is the difference between dry and flooded. Sea level is arguably the most
  ENSO-coupled, atoll-critical variable the app does not track at all.
* **Source:** AVISO/CMEMS satellite altimetry (free); NOAA CO-OPS tide gauges
  (free, but sparse in the FAS); PEAC also publishes a seasonal sea-level
  forecast (same nav as the rainfall outlook the app already scrapes).
* **Effort:** moderate–high (gridded altimetry is heavy). **Feasibility: high** for
  the PEAC outlook + altimetry point extraction.

title: Analysis Roadmap — Priority 4 — Cyclone impact (wind + surge), not just proximity
text:
* **What:** wind-impact estimate from JTWC quadrant wind radii (already ingested)
  + a storm-surge/inundation estimate using GEBCO bathymetry.
* **Why:** the app explicitly says "proximity only, no wind impact." For atolls,
  the actual damage is wind + overwash, which a nearest-track distance cannot
  express.
* **Source:** JTWC radii (have it), GEBCO bathymetry (`planned` in sources.yaml),
  a simple parametric wind field + storm-surge model.
* **Effort:** high. **Feasibility: medium** (surge modeling is the hard part; wind
  field is tractable).

title: Analysis Roadmap — Priority 5 — Forecast verification loop (closed)
text:
* **What:** score the Open-Meteo/ECMWF forecasts against observed (gauge/IMERG)
  rainfall each cycle, surface the skill.
* **Why:** the verification framework (bias/MAE/RMSE/skill) exists and is tested
  but is not run against live data. An unverified forecast in a decision tool
  quietly overstates confidence.
* **Source:** none new — combines #1 (gauge) with existing forecast + archive.
* **Effort:** low. **Feasibility: high.**

title: Analysis Roadmap — Priority 6 — ENSO → hazard coupling
text:
* **What:** cyclone frequency, sea-level anomaly, and SST/bleaching by ENSO phase
  (the analog engine already exists but has nothing to feed it).
* **Why:** turns "what is ENSO doing" into "what does ENSO mean here" — the
  El Niño drought linkage is partially done; cyclone and sea-level linkages are not.
* **Source:** IBTrACS + ONI (have), altimetry + SST (have the tiles, need the series).
* **Effort:** moderate. **Feasibility: high.**

title: Analysis Roadmap — Priority 7 — Alerting / decision support
text:
* **What:** push (Telegram/iMessage) when a drought index crosses a threshold, a
  cyclone approaches a location, or the PEAC index flips to Red.
* **Why:** the app is a dashboard; the FAS use case is *early warning*. The
  household already has a Telegram front door (ai-dev) this could reuse.
* **Source:** none new — thresholds + the existing alert engine + a notifier.
* **Effort:** low–moderate. **Feasibility: high.**

---

title: Analysis Roadmap — Suggested next three
text:
1. **GHCNd stations** (ground truth — unlocks verification + trust).
2. **SSEBop ET + water balance** (completes the drought monitor's other half).
3. **Sea-level anomaly + PEAC sea-level outlook** (the biggest un-modeled atoll
   hazard, and directly ENSO-coupled).

title: El Nino Drought Research — El Niño Droughts in the Freely Associated States — Research Synthesis
text:
> Compiled 2026-10-29 by a parallel research swarm (5 agents). Every figure is
> quoted from a cited source; nothing is invented. Where sources conflict, both
> values are shown. This is contextual research for COFA FORWARD's anticipatory
> drought intelligence — **not a forecast and not operational guidance.**

title: El Nino Drought Research — Bottom line
text:
The Freely Associated States (Palau, FSM, RMI) sit in the western-Pacific "warm
pool." During El Niño the Walker circulation's rising branch shifts east of the
date line, imposing **subsidence over the warm pool** and suppressing the deep
convection that produces the region's rainfall. The result is a recurring,
well-documented **drought that peaks in the dry season the year *after* a strong
El Niño** (the "El Niño Year +1" / post-peak phase). The region's **low coral
atolls** (most of the RMI, the FSM outer islands, Palau's remote atolls) are the
most vulnerable because they have no surface water and only a thin freshwater
lens + rain catchment.

**Immediate relevance (Oct 2026):** CPC's ENSO Diagnostic Discussion (8 Oct 2026)
is at **"El Niño Advisory"** — Niño-3.4 at **+2.1 °C** and strengthening, with a
strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through Jan–Mar 2027 and a 54–83% chance of a
*historic* event exceeding any since 1950. This is the drought precursor pattern.

title: El Nino Drought Research — The physical mechanism
text:
1. **Walker circulation shift.** El Niño moves the warm pool eastward; the rising
   (convective) branch of the Pacific Walker cell follows it east of 180°, and the
   sinking (subsidence) branch settles over the Maritime Continent / western warm
   pool (NOAA Climate.gov; Xiao et al. 2022, *Sci. Rep.*).
2. **ITCZ + SPCZ displacement.** The ITCZ shifts equatorward/eastward; the SPCZ
   shifts north and east (up to ~10° of latitude in strong events), leaving the
   FAS sector under the subsiding branch (Cai et al. 2012; Brown et al. 2021).
3. **Rainfall dipole.** The west Pacific dries while the central/eastern Pacific
   gets wetter. In Jan–Mar 1998 the western-Pacific rainfall total north of the
   equator was **<100 mm, >800 mm below normal** (CPC ENSO Rainfall).
4. **Lag.** Drought typically peaks **after** the El Niño peak — in the dry season
   of the following year (PEAC: "a very dry first-half of a calendar year is
   typical of the year following El Niño"). USGS: sharpest drought for Guam/Saipan/
   Chuuk arrives "the year after El Niño onset." Hydrological recovery can lag the
   rainfall recovery by years.

title: El Nino Drought Research — 1997–98 (strongest in local memory)
text:
- **Timing:** dry from late 1997 (outer islands from Oct); peak **Jan–May 1998**;
  Majuro drought ended **June 1998**.
- **Rainfall:** Majuro (RMI) got **8% of normal rain Jan–Apr 1998**. Jan 1998
  %-of-normal: Kolonia/Pingelap/Nukuoro (Pohnpei) 4–5%, Kosrae 9%, Weno 12%,
  Lukunoch (Chuuk) 3%, Kwajalein/Ebeye 8%, Wotje 18%, Saipan 25%, Koror 44%.
- **Gradient:** Pohnpei/Kosrae and the northern RMI atolls hardest; Palau was last
  to dry (Koror 44% in Jan); southern Palau (Peleliu) was wetter.
- **Crisis:** FSM + Pohnpei + Chuuk declared emergencies; ~28,800 people (~30% of
  outer-island population) needed relief; rivers dried, wells turned saline; taro
  failed; RMI drought disaster Feb 1998; Guam's worst drought (65% of normal annual
  rainfall, 12% of land scorched).

title: El Nino Drought Research — 2015–16 (super El Niño, record ONI)
text:
- **Timing:** onset Jan–Jun 2015, peak Jul 2015–Feb 2016; drought rainfall deficits
  from **OND 2015**, worst **Jan–Apr 2016**, recovery Apr–Aug 2016 (Palau's
  accumulated deficit bottomed −85.73 in in Aug 2016).
- **Rainfall (% normal):** Q4 2015 — Majuro 39%, Yap 40%, Palau 46%, Kosrae 52%;
  Q1 2016 — Kwajalein 18%, Majuro 27%, Yap 35%, Palau 55%. Koror got ~1/3 of normal
  from 1 Mar 2016 and its lowest 4-month total since 1951.
- **Gradient:** west + north hardest (Palau, Yap, northern RMI atolls); Chuuk less
  affected; Pohnpei/Kosrae had big relative shortfalls from a very wet baseline;
  American Samoa was anomalously *wet* (127–137%).
- **Crisis:** FSM emergency 18 Feb 2016; RMI emergency 3 Feb → disaster 8/10 Mar
  (extended twice); **Obama FEMA disaster declaration for RMI 27 Apr 2016** (only
  FAS country to request international aid); Palau EO-389 21/22 Mar 2016 — Ngerimel
  Dam dried, Koror/Airai on 3 hr/day rationing; ~21,000 affected in RMI, ~100,000
  in FSM; RMI deployed 55 RO units / 33 communities.

title: El Nino Drought Research — 2023–24 (strong, but weaker than the two above)
text:
- **Timing:** declared Jul 2023, peak Dec 2023–Jan 2024 (ONI ~+2.0 °C), neutral by
  mid-2024.
- **Impact:** **FSM national emergency 11 Mar 2024** (~22,700 people, ~20% of
  population; Yap/Ulithi reached **D4 exceptional drought**; Yap's Mar–Apr rain was
  2nd-driest in 73 years). **RMI** severe drought ~5,200 people (Wotje D4) but **no
  national disaster declaration**. **Palau mostly spared** (Stage 1 / abnormal
  dryness only).
- **Comparison:** FSM/SPREP: impacts "unlikely to match" 1997–98 or 2015–16.

title: El Nino Drought Research — Which areas are most affected, and why
text:
| Tier | Areas | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Most vulnerable** | Northern RMI atolls (Wotje, Utrik, Ailuk, Mejit, Likiep, Maloelap, Wotho, Ujae…); FSM outer atolls (Yap's Ulithi/Woleai/Fais; Chuuk's Mortlocks; Pohnpei's southern atolls); Palau's Kayangel/Sonsorol/Hatohobei | No surface water; thin lens; rain catchment only. RMI: 55% of islands have lens <2.5 m; islands <300 m wide fully depleted in 1998 drought (Barkey & Bailey 2017). |
| **Driest high island** | Yap Proper (~122 in/yr; streams dry ~3 mo/yr) vs Pohnpei (~190 in/yr) | Lower baseline rainfall; intermittent streams. |
| **More resilient** | Pohnpei, Kosrae, Chuuk Lagoon high islands, Palau's Babeldaob | Rainfall + perennial streams/rivers (Babeldaob has Palau's only perennial rivers + Lake Ngardok). |
| **Surprising failure point** | Palau's Koror (limestone, dam-dependent) | Ngerimel Dam dried up in 2016 despite national streams. |

text:
- RMI ~55–58,000 total; Majuro ~20,000+; 2013 northern-atoll drought ~6,400 people

title: Usgs Drought Import — Verified drought-classification method (from `3_IMERG_Monthly_Drought_Monitor.R`)
text:
Four indices, all computed against the **2000–2024 baseline**:

1. **1-/3-/6-Month Rainfall Index** — quintile class of the monthly precipitation
   and its right-aligned rolling 3-/6-month sums, each vs the same-calendar-month
   distribution: `<20th→Drier, <40th→Dry, <60th→Typical, <80th→Wet, ≥80th→Wetter`.
2. **PEAC 4/8-inch Index** — absolute traffic light on the latest month:
   `<101.6 mm→Red (drought concern), 101.6–203.2 mm→Yellow (adequate),
   >203.2 mm→Dark Green (sufficient)`.

The app's `drought/percentiles.quintile_index` and `drought/percentiles.peac_index`
reproduce these thresholds exactly; `drought/monitor.py` computes all four indices.

title: Immediate Drought Response Plan for the Republic of the Marshall Islands
text: Immediate Drought Response Plan for the Republic of the Marshall Islands. Complementing the Declaration on State of Emergency (3 Feb 2016) for the 2015–16 El Niño drought. Covers a 6-month WASH-focused response across 19 atolls/islands, 44 communities, ~1,257 households plus 4,092 in Majuro. State of Emergency declared 3 February 2016. Vulnerability zoning: Zone 1 (>8°N) high, Zone 2 (6°–8°N) high, Zone 3 (<6°N) moderate (Mili Atoll raised to Zone 2). Northern atolls (Zone 1/2) are the government-designated highest-vulnerability area — matches the app's northern-atoll finding. El Niño rainfall pattern: above-average early year, dry from Nov–Dec, returning ~July. Response: drinking-water distribution points, reverse-osmosis units, safe-water education.

title: RMI Response Plan for Drought and Inundation (RPDI) 2024
text: RMI Response Plan for Drought and Inundation (RPDI) 2024. The 2024 drought + inundation response plan. In early 2024, 18 atolls were impacted by inundation and drought affected ~15,000 people (~35%) across 23 atolls/islands; NDMO deployed RO units to 9 of 16 affected atolls. NDMO deployed Reverse-Osmosis units to 9 of 16 drought-affected atolls (2024). ~5,200 people (12.3% of population) affected across 15 atolls/islands. Three schools without RO units were forced to close. 18 atolls impacted by inundation on 20 Jan and 9–10 Mar 2024.

title: FSM National Drought Preparedness and Response Plan (NDPRP)
text: FSM National Drought Preparedness and Response Plan (NDPRP). FSM's first comprehensive national drought framework, endorsed 22 Aug 2026. Three pillars: (1) early warning systems, (2) vulnerability & impact assessment, (3) mitigation, preparedness & response. Coordinates national, state, municipal and community actors. Endorsed 22 August 2026 (the current national framework). Three pillars: early warning; vulnerability/impact assessment; mitigation–preparedness–response. Historical drought events: 1983, 1998, 2015–16, and 2023–24 El Niño. National emergency declared 12 March 2024 (President Simina) for Pohnpei/Yap/Chuuk; $1.2M; 21,000+ in urgent need.

title: Palau National Drought Action Plan
text: Palau National Drought Action Plan. Palau's stage-based drought action plan. The National Emergency Committee activates stages; NEMO issues public advisories. Stage 1 is the water-shortage watch (entered 26 March 2024 during the 2023–24 El Niño). Stage 1 = water-shortage watch; activated 26 March 2024. NEC activates stages based on National Weather Service monitoring; NEMO issues advisories. Stage definitions are stage-based (watch → warning → emergency) rather than rainfall-percentile based.

title: Drought Emergency Response for the North Pacific (FSM and RMI)
text: Drought Emergency Response for the North Pacific (FSM and RMI). UNICEF's response to the 2023–24 El Niño drought in FSM and RMI: WASH kits, RO support, health/nutrition, education continuity, and child protection. FSM: >21,000 in urgent need; saltwater intrusion in Lekinioch/Piherarh/Onoun (Chuuk lagoon). RMI: >5,200 people (12.3%) affected across 15 atolls/islands; little/no rain for 2–3 months. 4,307 WASH kits planned; 12 collapsible water tanks; water filters + school WASH.

title: Open-Meteo Forecast API
text: Open-Meteo Forecast API. Publisher Open-Meteo. Global; covers Palau, FSM, RMI points temperature_2m, precipitation, wind_speed_10m, wind_direction_10m, relative_humidity_2m, surface_pressure, ...

title: Open-Meteo Marine API (waves + sea-surface temperature)
text: Open-Meteo Marine API (waves + sea-surface temperature). Publisher Open-Meteo. Global ocean (covers FAS points) significant wave height/period/direction, sea-surface temperature Feeds the coastal/marine conditions + the simplified coral-bleaching watch (Degree Heating Weeks).

title: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API (ERA5-based)
text: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API (ERA5-based). Publisher Open-Meteo / ECMWF ERA5. Global precipitation_sum, temperature_2m_mean

title: NOAA CPC Oceanic Niño Index (ONI)
text: NOAA CPC Oceanic Niño Index (ONI). Publisher NOAA Climate Prediction Center. Niño-3.4 index (basin-scale; no per-island data) ONI SST anomaly (the canonical ENSO index) Authoritative machine-readable ENSO index. Phase label is derived via the CPC >=5-season criterion; the official status statement is the Diagnostic Discussion.

title: PEAC seasonal rainfall outlook (tercile consensus)
text: PEAC seasonal rainfall outlook (tercile consensus). Publisher NOAA NWS Pacific ENSO Applications Climate Services. 14 stations: Hawaii, USAPI (Palau/FSM/RMI), Guam/CNMI, American Samoa tercile rainfall probabilities (below:near:above), final outlook per station HTML scrape of the official experimental consensus outlook (7 seasonal models, tercile form). FAS stations carry a geo_id. FRESHNESS GUARD: last updated 2024-09-16 (SON 2024) — the Pacific ENSO Update newsletter is discontinued and the outlook has gone stale; the adapter flags is_stale so the app presents it as historical, never as current.

title: University of Hawaii Sea Level Center (UHSLC) tide gauges
text: University of Hawaii Sea Level Center (UHSLC) tide gauges. Publisher University of Hawaii / NOAA. 6 FAS tide gauges: Malakal (Palau), Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, Kwajalein, Majuro (no Kosrae) sea level (mm above station datum) Authoritative current tide-gauge source. Replaces the PEAC seasonal sea-level outlook, which was DISCONTINUED January 2020. Sea level is the most ENSO-coupled atoll hazard (El Nino raises western-Pacific sea level -> king-tide/inundation flooding). Data availability varies by station.

title: NOAA CPC ENSO Diagnostic Discussion
text: NOAA CPC ENSO Diagnostic Discussion. Publisher NOAA Climate Prediction Center. Global ENSO state + official probabilistic outlook ENSO Alert System status, synopsis, outlook summary HTML scrape of the official status statement: issue date, alert status (e.g. El Niño Advisory), synopsis, outlook summary. Authoritative (not a derived phase).

title: IBTrACS v04r01 (International Best Track Archive)
text: IBTrACS v04r01 (International Best Track Archive). Publisher NOAA/NCEI. Western North Pacific basin (covers Palau/FSM/RMI) position, WMO wind/pressure (JMA 10-min for WP), per-agency wind (USA/Tokyo), radii

title: JMA RSMC Tokyo-Typhoon Center (active storms)
text: JMA RSMC Tokyo-Typhoon Center (active storms). Publisher Japan Meteorological Agency. Western North Pacific (RSMC Tokyo AOR; covers all FAS) position, central pressure, 10-min sustained wind, gusts, 30/50-kt radii, forecast track + probability circles Authoritative active-storm source (WMO RSMC). JSON endpoints, no auth.

title: JTWC tropical cyclone warnings
text: JTWC tropical cyclone warnings. Publisher Joint Typhoon Warning Center (via NWS text mirror). NW Pacific (covers FAS) 1-min sustained wind, quadrant wind radii (34/50/64 kt), MSLP, forecast track ATCF-style text warnings parsed into structured data (position, 1-min wind, radii, forecast). Complements JMA (10-min wind).

title: JMA Himawari-9 geostationary satellite imagery
text: JMA Himawari-9 geostationary satellite imagery. Publisher JMA / NICT. Full disk (80E–160W; FAS in western-Pacific portion) visible composite imagery Full-disk composite shown in the app (Tropical Cyclones page). IR bands and region zoom tiles are a follow-up.

title: NWS Guam / PEAC (FAS watches & warnings)
text: NWS Guam / PEAC (FAS watches & warnings). Publisher NOAA NWS Pacific Region. Marianas + Micronesia (Palau, FSM, RMI island-specific) storm identity, island-level watches/warnings TCP text parsed (storm + watches/warnings). api.weather.gov/alerts also available for structured zone alerts. The only source that turns JTWC/JMA guidance into FAS island-specific actions.

title: NASA GPM IMERG precipitation (Final/Late/Early)
text: NASA GPM IMERG precipitation (Final/Late/Early). Publisher NASA GES DISC. 60N-60S (covers FAS, over ocean + land) precipitationCal, randomError, probabilityLiquidPrecipitation earthaccess adapter (ingestion/imerg.py) for daily point extraction; live-verified (token auth + search + download + extraction). Requires EARTHDATA_TOKEN (or ~/.netrc) and a one-time GPM IMERG EULA acceptance.

title: CHIRPS v3 precipitation (UCSB Climate Hazards Center)
text: CHIRPS v3 precipitation (UCSB Climate Hazards Center). Publisher UC Santa Barbara. 60N-60S (land-masked; tiny atolls may be sparse) precip (mm) Point extraction via COG range requests (rasterio /vsicurl). Land-masked; sub-pixel islands use a documented max-valid-pixel heuristic. ERA5 preferred for ocean-adjacent atolls.

title: USGS SSEBop actual evapotranspiration (FEWS NET monthly)
text: USGS SSEBop actual evapotranspiration (FEWS NET monthly). Publisher USGS EROS. Global land (~1 km) — tiny atolls fall in ocean (nodata) pixels actual evapotranspiration (mm/month) Actual ET (the complement to Hargreaves PET). Land-only — valid for high islands (Pohnpei/Kosrae/Yap/Weno/Babeldaob), unavailable for tiny atolls. ~73 MB/month; sampled with the max-valid-pixel heuristic.

title: PERSIANN-CDR precipitation (NOAA CDR)
text: PERSIANN-CDR precipitation (NOAA CDR). Publisher NOAA NCEI / UC Irvine CHRS. 60S-60N (covers FAS, over ocean + land) precipitation (mm) Daily point extraction via NCEI HTTP (per-file download + xarray). Satellite-gauge blend; covers ocean-adjacent atolls (CHIRPS is land-masked). Lags ~3-6 months (CDR).

title: GPCC monthly gauge precipitation
text: GPCC monthly gauge precipitation. Publisher DWD (Deutscher Wetterdienst). Land only — essentially no gauges on FAS islands (not recommended) precip, numgauge Not a primary FAS source (no local gauges).

title: SPEIbase (global standardized precipitation-evapotranspiration index)
text: SPEIbase (global standardized precipitation-evapotranspiration index). Publisher CSIC. Global land 0.5 deg — many FAS atolls fall between cells (NaN) SPEI Coarse; better to compute SPI/SPEI ourselves from CHIRPS/IMERG.

title: NMME seasonal forecasts (multi-model ensemble)
text: NMME seasonal forecasts (multi-model ensemble). Publisher NOAA/NCEP + partners. Global 1 deg (FAS falls within grid cells) prate, tmp2m, tmpsfc (NetCDF3) xarray + netCDF4 point extraction of ENSMEAN across 6 models; ensemble mean/spread. 1-deg grid is coarse for atolls.

title: ECMWF AIFS open data (AI forecast)
text: ECMWF AIFS open data (AI forecast). Publisher ECMWF. Global 0.25 deg (covers FAS) 2m temp/dewpoint, 10m wind, total precipitation, MSLP, pressure levels (GRIB2) Best free AI/global model drop-in (GRIB2). See docs.

title: NOAA GFS / GEFS (NOMADS / AWS NODD)
text: NOAA GFS / GEFS (NOMADS / AWS NODD). Publisher NOAA/NCEP. Global 0.25 deg full GRIB2 forecast fields

title: USGS Drought Monitoring & 7-Day Precip Forecasting, Western Pacific (2000-2026)
text: USGS Drought Monitoring & 7-Day Precip Forecasting, Western Pacific (2000-2026). Publisher USGS EROS. 9 sites across FSM, RMI, Nauru, Solomon Islands — PALAU NOT INCLUDED monthly precip, 25-yr climatological median, rolling 1/3/6-month, quintile Rainfall Index (Drier/Dry/Typical/Wet/Wetter), PEAC thresholds, 7-day GFS forecast METHODOLOGY REPLICATED LOCALLY: the app computes the same indicators (monthly precip, climatological median, rolling 1/3/6-month, quintile Rainfall Index + D0-D4) from ERA5/CHIRPS in drought/monitor.py — an independent implementation of Senay et al. 2026 (the USGS pipeline runs on IMERG Early Run). The USGS CSV itself remains ScienceBase/Cloudflare-gated (403 to curl); the exact station-specific PEAC absolute thresholds are in its R scripts (blocked). Covers FSM/RMI/Nauru/Solomon only — Palau is not in the release.

title: WorldPop population grids (Unconstrained individual countries)
text: WorldPop population grids (Unconstrained individual countries). Publisher University of Southampton. Global 2000-2020 (covers PLW/FSM/MHL at ~1km) population count (UN-adjusted) Point/radius extraction (rasterio). UN-adjusted 2020 totals exceed censuses; used for spatial exposure, not census of record.

title: GPWv4 population (SEDAC)
text: GPWv4 population (SEDAC). Publisher NASA SEDAC / CIESIN. Global (covers FAS) population count, density

title: HDX Common Operational Dataset administrative boundaries
text: HDX Common Operational Dataset administrative boundaries. Publisher OCHA / ITOS / SPC. FSM (4 states, 75 municipalities) and RMI (25 atolls, 153 EAs). Palau: no COD-AB. administrative boundaries (SHP), P-coded Loaded via pyshp + rasterio (no GDAL/geopandas). Enables accurate zonal WorldPop population. Palau: see geoboundaries source (no COD-AB).

title: geoBoundaries administrative boundaries (Palau ADM1)
text: geoBoundaries administrative boundaries (Palau ADM1). Publisher William & Mary geoLab (OpenStreetMap-derived). Palau ADM1 (16 states) administrative boundaries (GeoJSON) Parsed with stdlib json. Used for Palau zonal population (Palau has no COD-AB).

title: Copernicus DEM GLO-30/GLO-90 (terrain)
text: Copernicus DEM GLO-30/GLO-90 (terrain). Publisher Copernicus / Sinergise (AWS Open Data). GLO-90 worldwide (covers FAS); GLO-30 limited (verify tiles) surface elevation

title: GEBCO global bathymetry + topography
text: GEBCO global bathymetry + topography. Publisher GEBCO. Global ocean + land (covers FAS) elevation + bathymetry Use for atoll coastal/storm-surge exposure.

title: Google WeatherNext 3
text: Google WeatherNext 3. Publisher Google. Global 0.05/0.1/0.25 deg full forecast fields (Zarr v3 / BigQuery / Earth Engine) Allowlist-gated GCS buckets (gs://weathernext3_spatial). Adapter implemented; reads Zarr via gcsfs once credentials + allowlist are present. Access form submitted (see docs). ECMWF AIFS / GFS are the working free alternatives in the meantime.

title: NVIDIA Earth-2 / FourCastNet / StormCast
text: NVIDIA Earth-2 / FourCastNet / StormCast. Publisher NVIDIA. Global 0.25 deg (FourCastNet); 3-km regional (StormCast/CorrDiff) 2m temp, 10m wind, MSLP, TP, 500hPa geopotential No keyless free hosted weather API. FourCastNet/StormCast are downloadable open weights (self-host on GPU via Modulus); hosted NIM weather microservices need a paid NVIDIA API key / DGX Cloud. Adapter implemented and honestly reports unavailable without a key.

title: Windy
text: Windy. Publisher Windy.com. Global  No free public API. Model data (ECMWF/GFS/ICON/GEM) already integrated via Open-Meteo multi-model.

title: Weather Underground
text: Weather Underground. Publisher Weather Underground (IBM/The Weather Company). Global  The free WU API was shut down. Use Open-Meteo / GFS / METAR alternatives instead.

title: Meteoconsult (MétéoConsult)
text: Meteoconsult (MétéoConsult). Publisher Meteoconsult / La Chaîne Météo. Primarily Europe  No public free API and minimal Pacific coverage. Meteoblue has a free non-commercial API if a European NWP alternative is wanted.

title: NOAA US Drought Monitor (USDM)
text: NOAA US Drought Monitor (USDM). Publisher NOAA/NDMC/USDA. US + territories only — does NOT cover Palau/FSM/RMI  USDM is US-only. The app instead computes a precipitation-percentile D0–D4 drought level (internal FAS scale) and uses CHIRPS/IMERG/ERA5 for drought indicators. USGS western-Pacific product (P1RXUMV3) covers FSM/RMI (planned).

title: NOAA GOES geostationary imagery
text: NOAA GOES geostationary imagery. Publisher NOAA. GOES-West full disk covers ~eastern Pacific / Americas — the FAS (130–175E) is in Himawari's domain, not GOES's  Not a good fit for the FAS — Himawari-9 (implemented) is the correct geostationary satellite. GOES is only marginally useful for the far-eastern RMI (~172E).

title: Copernicus Sentinel-2/3
text: Copernicus Sentinel-2/3. Publisher ESA / Copernicus. Global (FAS included)  Ocean/land remote sensing (SST, ocean colour, vegetation), not weather feeds. STAC search over AWS s3://sentinel-* or the CDS; heavy raster. A follow-up for SST/coastal overlays.

title: NASA/NOAA VIIRS (SNPP/NOAA-20/21)
text: NASA/NOAA VIIRS (SNPP/NOAA-20/21). Publisher NASA / NOAA. Global (FAS included)  SST/ocean-colour/vegetation remote sensing via Earthdata (LANCE/LAADS). Heavy raster; a follow-up if SST monitoring is wanted.

title: NASA GIBS remote-sensing overlays (MUR SST, SST anomaly, PACE chlorophyll-a)
text: NASA GIBS remote-sensing overlays (MUR SST, SST anomaly, PACE chlorophyll-a). Publisher NASA EOSDIS / JPL. Global ocean (FAS included) sea-surface temperature, SST anomaly, chlorophyll-a concentration Toggleable map overlays (semi-transparent WMTS tiles) drawn over the satellite basemap. Remote-sensing fields, NOT forecast or in-situ station data. SST anomaly is relative to a MUR climatology and is relevant to ENSO monitoring.
